note.announcementTitle: Board Meeting Outcome for Outcome Of Board Meeting
note.headline: Rs319.6cr GST provision swings Delta Corp standalone Q2FY27 to a loss -- SC casino-tax demand crystallizes far below the Rs16,823cr+ show-cause ceiling
thesisChain: Supreme Court's 27-May-2026 judgment on GST applicability to casino/online-gaming settles the valuation basis for long-pending show-cause notices (originally up to ~Rs16,823cr + Rs6,384cr + Rs1,884cr across entities/periods)
Adjudication orders under Rule 31C determine actual casino-transaction GST demand at Rs78.56cr and mixed-supply demand at Rs93.80cr for Jul2017-Mar2022

Extending the same basis through Sep2023 (casino) and Sep2025 (mixed supply), the company books a cumulative Rs319.60cr provision (incl. interest) in standalone results -- Rs200.62cr already taken in Q1FY27, the balance now in Q2FY27
Standalone Q2FY27 EPS swings to Rs(2.99) vs +Rs0.84 in Q2FY26; H1FY27 EPS is Rs(7.07) vs +Rs1.80 in H1FY26

Company has already paid ~Rs49cr principal post-quarter under the Rule 31C order, intends to contest the balance, and separately no longer needs to indemnify Head Digital Works for DGL's GST exposure -- a related contingent-liability removal

epsImpact.magnitude: Q2FY27 standalone EPS swings to ~Rs(2.99) from +Rs0.84 YoY on a one-time Rs319.6cr exceptional GST provision; H1FY27 EPS Rs(7.07) vs +Rs1.80 YoY

note.insight: Formal Regulation 30 filing (Board Meeting Outcome + full standalone financial results enclosed). This is a FOLLOW-UP that quantifies a risk already flagged at 'high' significance on 28-Sep-2026 (then a Rs116.4cr differential demand) -- today's filing shows the actual P&L hit is larger: a cumulative Rs319.60cr GST provision (including interest) across Q1+Q2 FY27, driven by Supreme Court-settled adjudication orders on casino (Rs78.56cr) and mixed-supply (Rs93.80cr) GST for Jul2017-Mar2022, extended through later periods. This swings standalone Q2FY27 to a loss (EPS Rs(2.99) vs +Rs0.84 a year ago) and H1FY27 to EPS Rs(7.07) vs +Rs1.80. Importantly, the final adjudicated/provisioned numbers (Rs319.6cr total) are dramatically smaller than the theoretical worst case the original show-cause notices implied (north of Rs16,800cr across entities), so this is also a tail-risk de-risking event even though it drives this quarter's headline loss; the company has already paid ~Rs49cr principal and plans to contest the remainder, and a related indemnity obligation to Head Digital Works (DGL buyer) has fallen away. Watch for: further adjudication orders covering the extended Sep2023/Sep2025 periods, and whether litigation reduces the provisioned amount in a future quarter.
